Observable verification action: Before committing, find a current-image observation or tool result that directly addresses plane/orientation for the same image. A frontal chest projection showing both lungs, heart, and spine en face supports the coronal plane; an axial cross-sectional slice supports the transverse plane. Confirm the terminal answer uses that observed orientation evidence, not just the released reference or a correct grade. If no observation or tool result addresses orientation, retrieve or rerun orientation verification and treat the answer as unconfirmed until then. If options are displayed, map the supported plane text back to the displayed choice and check that its letter and text agree; if the option map is empty, skip letter mapping. In this case, the transcript had no observations or tool calls and an empty option map, so “Yes” matching the reference does not prove the procedure; the rationale described a frontal chest radiograph, but no current-image verification was supplied.
